You can't be addicted to the internet. Here's how it works:

You spend your time doing hobbies when you aren't doing work/school. Some hobbies are fulfilling, others are not. In school majority of my hobbies landed on a computer. I recorded music, I made videos, I wrote novels, I played videogames, and of course I can't forget all my favorite online friends. All my hobbies basically meant I was on a computer majority of the day.

If you feel unfulfilled or depressed, the first thing you should always do is change up some hobbies and try replacing one with another. While yes, I do spend a massive amount of time in front of screens (doesn't help that I'm now a computer science major), I do have balance. I work out regularly and I'm in good shape. I bring my dog on daily walks. I take a weekend each month to hang out with a friend who lives 40 minutes from my house where we ride her horses and go on adventures.

If you're asking if you are addicted to the internet, I think you're hitting a patch where you are beginning to feel like you're wasting too much time. The solution isn't to randomly use the computer less. You need to pick up a new hobby and add it into your schedule. Open a business where you put two hours a day into making something you can sell, force yourself to go out with a friend once a month, get a part-time job three days a week and start saving up money, get a dog and use Pokemon GO as an excuse to walk it 1-2KMs a day. Keep trying new things until you start feeling good with the direction you're taking.
